Joe Burrow did not mince words about avoiding a 0-2 division record: "We want to be 4-2 and controlling our own destiny." Baltimore has taken five of the last six meetings in this rivalry, including a 24-0 shutout last winter. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's game. Dexter Lawrence Sacks the Quarterback Twice Cincinnati brought in All-Pro tackle Dexter Lawrence to make life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Lawrence shares the team sack lead with three, anchoring a defensive front that brings down passers on 10.12% of attempts. Baltimore's reshuffled offensive line gives him another opportunity to take over. Cam Jurgens is set to make his Ravens debut at center after recovering from a concussion, pushing Vega Ioane over to right guard. That leaves Jurgens with a difficult first assignment against Cincinnati's 340-pound anchor. Lawrence will dominate the A-gap, dropping Baltimore's signal-caller twice and collapsing the pocket before deep plays can develop. Tee Higgins Explodes for Over 100 Yards and Two Touchdowns Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins (5) and wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (1) celebrate a Higgins touchdown in the second quarter of the NFL Week 3 game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh on Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. The game was tied at 17 at halftime. Baltimore's secondary will have its hands full matching up on the perimeter. Ja'Marr Chase usually attracts plenty of attention from opposing defenses. That could leave Tee Higgins with more opportunities to exploit one-on-one coverage on the outside. Zac Taylor called Higgins a "major weapon" outside, pointing out that his past production against Baltimore often gets overlooked. Baltimore loves flooding the field with six defensive backs, but smaller defensive backs cannot match Higgins' massive frame . Burrow is going to test those 50-50 balls down the sideline, letting Higgins sprint his way to 100 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Jordan Battle Jumps a Route for Another Takeaway Jordan Battle is playing like a ball-hawking magnet right now. He shares the NFL lead with three interceptions after picking off two passes in Miami , and Taylor said this week that "turnovers scream at you" in division dogfights. Baltimore's passing attack has hit dead ends late in games, going scoreless in the second half three times. Backup Tyler Huntley averages just six yards a pop, while Lamar Jackson is working through a sore ankle. Battle will bait a throw over the middle, jump the passing lane, and flip the field with another huge takeaway. Boye Mafe and the Front Stop Derrick Henry Under 60 Yards Derrick Henry leads the league in rushing scores, but Cincinnati's rebuilt front is ready for the challenge. Taylor praised Mafe's work against the run earlier this week, saying that the defensive end's "willingness to set an edge and win in the run game is equally as critical as being able to rush the passer." Mafe and Cincinnati's front will swarm the boundary on early downs. By stacking the box and sealing outside lanes, Cincinnati will limit Henry to under 60 yards. There have been reports the last two weeks that Jackson has a chance to play through his ankle injury, but he has not suited up in practice -- or for a game -- since Week 4. (AP Photo/Al Behrman) Ravens Bengals Week 7 Opponent Preview Scouting Report Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE Michael Hull Digital Coordinator Fresh off a Week 6 bye, the Cincinnati Bengals head to Baltimore for an AFC North battle with the Ravens. Baltimore is coming off a 13-10 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6 and sits at 4-2 on the year. The Ravens offense ranks seventh in the NFL with 26 points per game and eighth with 367.7 yards per game under new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. Franchise QB Lamar Jackson has missed the last two games with an ankle injury, and backup Tyler Huntley has led the Ravens to a 1-1 record in Jackson's absence. First-year Head Coach Jesse Minter said Monday he is unsure if Jackson returns to practice or plays this week against the Bengals. "I'd still put it in kind of the day-to-day thing," Minter said. "We'll know a lot more on Wednesday, I would say." When he has been on the field, Jackson has completed 70.8% of his passes (68-of-96) for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception. Meanwhile, Huntley has also completed 70.8% of his passes (51-of-72) for 429 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. The offense has been less vertical in two games with Huntley: Jackson leads all quarterbacks with at least 25 attempts in average yards per attempt (10.1) this season, while Huntley ranks 35th among 43 QBs (6.0), per NFL NextGenStats. RB Derrick Henry continues to defy Father Time as he leads the NFL in carries (130), is tied for first in rushing touchdowns (seven) and is fourth in rushing yards (534) in his age-32 season. He also forced 29 missed tackles, the sixth most in the league. WR Zay Flowers again leads the Baltimore receiving room. Despite missing Week 2, Flowers ranks ninth in the NFL with 471 receiving yards. Among 218 pass catchers to run at least 50 routes this season, Flowers ranks first in yards per route run (3.8). In two matchups with the Bengals last year, CB DJ Turner II matched up with Flowers 21 times, allowing one catch for 14 yards on four targets, per NGS. Help us honor 2026 Ring of Honor inductees James Brooks and Bob Trumpy at halftime against the Tennessee Titans on Nov. 1! Baltimore is allowing 22 points per game defensively, the 15th fewest in the NFL, and giving up 310.8 yards per game, the 12th fewest. Former Bengal Trey Hendrickson highlights the Baltimore defense, ranking in the top 12 in QB pressures with 25 so far this season. Hendrickson returned from injury in last week's loss to the Browns to record eight pressures and a sack. home.headline: Bengals' Erick All suffers injury vs. Ravens
home.blurb: This story will be updated with more information as it becomes available. UPDATE: The Bengals ruled All out for the game due to a knee injury. Cincinnati Bengals tight end Erick All suffered an injury during his team’s Week 7 game against the Baltimore Ravens. All was an important part of the team’s second-half comeback before exiting with an injury. As seen on the broadcast, All limped off the field and went to the blue medical tent, then eventually went to the locker room. All has been a critical part of the offense for the Bengals when healthy, but his serious injury history that knocked his draft stock down appears to be popping up again. The Bengals already put Tanner Hudson on injured reserve this season, so depth behind Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample continues to look shaky. picks.blurb: Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New York Giants might have a winning record (3-2-1) right now and lead the NFC East. But let’s be honest. Aside from their dominant Week 1 showing against the Dallas Cowboys, have the Giants really looked as good as their record suggests? We’re talking about a team where the phrase “A win’s a win” applies. The Giants barely beat the Tennessee Titans, 12-7, in Week 3. They also had to fight back in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals, who led 24-19 at one point. The tie against the Commanders? That one was a gift. If Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn don’t have that brain blip, the Commanders likely win, despite the Giants roaring back from a 19-6 deficit. And last week? We’re sorry, but the Giants had no business losing to the New Orleans Saints as badly as they did. And again, make no mistake: the Giants lost that game because they were their own worst enemy, as shown by the sloppy play they put on film. But it’s funny how the football gods work. The Giants, regardless of what they do against the Houston Texans this week, will remain in first place in the division. They have a chance, albeit a difficult one, to get back to looking like the team they were in Week 1, even though they’ve since lost a lot of key personnel, all of whom played in that win: quarterback Jaxson Dart, returner/receiver Braxton Berrios, outside linebacker Brian Burns, and inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds. So what’s the goal this week if the Giants want to pull off an upset win over the Texans on the road? “We’ve been practicing well the last few weeks,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “I think practice has been improving every single week, which is the mark of a team that has got a chance to do something. You’ve got to keep improving. “So, we are on track to do that. I’m looking forward to it showing up in terms of consistency. If we’ve been anything, we’ve been inconsistent.” It’s really that simple. The question is, will the Giants finally find the consistency that’s eluded them since that Week 1 game? Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans The Texans might be on a roll, having won their last two games, but they still have a few flaws that could work to the Giants’ advantage. For one, the Texans’ offensive line ranks 27th in the PFF pass-blocking efficiency rating metric. The unit has allowed 71 quarterback pressures, tied for third-most in the league. Left tackle Aireontae Ersery has allowed 20 quarterback pressures, per PFF, tied for fourth-most in the league among left tackles. Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has turned up the heat on opposing quarterbacks in recent weeks. This year, opposing quarterbacks have completed only 54.1% of their pass attempts against the Giants’ blitz, the fourth-lowest completion rate in the league. Of course, the key is for the Giants to stop the run, something they haven’t done consistently in recent weeks. So we’ll see if Wilson’s calling out his defensive players for not running to the ball lights a fire underneath them. Offensively, the Giants need to get their running game going, and the hope is that switching to quarterback J.J. McCarthy will help. This more mobile quarterback will discourage the Texans from loading up the box and start accounting for McCarthy as a runner. More importantly, McCarthy’s ability to scramble away from trouble could help the Giants’ ailing offensive tackles, Andrew Thomas and, if he plays, Jermaine Eluemunor, against that Texans pass rush. Per Next Gen Stats, since 2025, McCarthy has scrambled 19 times for 185 yards and three touchdowns, a 9.7 yards-per-carry average, which is a league high among quarterbacks with a minimum of 15 carries. If McCarthy can buy time, he stands a chance at connecting with receiver Malik Nabers or tight end Isaiah Likely, both of whom have been the most frequently targeted players on offense for the Giants over the last few weeks. Why the Giants Will Lose to the Texans I touched on it a bit above, but I’ll say it again here. The Giants have to stop the run. Texans’ top running back, David Montgomery, has been sidelined with a groin injury, but Woody Marks has stepped up in his place. Marks is an explosive running back who has averaged almost four yards per rush over the last two weeks. He also has six catches for 47 yards over that span. The Giants’ run defense? Not good at all. Big Blue has allowed opponents 135.5 rushing yards per game this year, and their 5.0 yards per carry allowed is the second-worst average in the league. If the Giants can’t stuff Marks and the Texans’ running game, it won’t matter what pass-rush plan they have this week. And until the unit shows it has cleaned up the missed tackles (13 last week, seven against the run per PFF), that aspect of the game will remain the team’s Achilles heel. At the start of the season, I had this game down as a loss and nothing — not even the Texans’ 2-4 record or the Giants’ 3-2-1 start — has changed my mind. The Texans have been coming into their own lately, and the Giants, aside from their Week 1 win over Dallas, have barely gotten by in their other wins and in their tie against Washington. The Giants will fight — that much I am certain of — and I hope this doesn’t turn into the ugly rout that I fear it could become. And the pieces could certainly be in place for the Texans to make that third consecutive win become a reality. Their offense is looking the best it has all season after another strong performance from C.J. Stroud. The defense will have the task of facing a new starting quarterback on the other side in J.J. McCarthy , and all of that coming back on Houston's home field tends to make their chances look even better. And when looking at the Texans' betting odds heading into Week 7, it's becoming pretty clear that the sportsbooks have one obvious favorite in mind for this weekend's action in Houston. Texans Already Projected to Rout the Giants in Week 7 According to recent odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are now listed as 10.5-point favorites (-550 ML) over the Giants in Week 7. That's by far the Texans' highest spread heading into any week they've played this season. And when looking around the league's Week 7 matchups, Houston is currently the only team listed as a favorite by more than a touchdown––let alone being a favorite by double digits. Stroud (7) celebrates his touchdown with wide receiver Nico Collins (12) against the Tennessee Titans during the second half at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. So if the Texans are projected to win by double-digits, and the total score isn't expected to reach above 43 points, that's not much of an optimistic statement from the books on how this Giants offense could fare against a Houston defensive unit that many considered among the best in the NFL heading into this season. Will the Texans Actually Dominate the Giants as Expected? Now, projections are one thing. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants. But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition? Really, it all relies upon the defense. Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show. away.headline: New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything
away.blurb: This will also make New York a step slower in its front seven, which will not only affect the pass rush (Edmunds actually has a couple of sacks this season), but also its pass coverage, which was already questionable. New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As if the New York Giants didn't already have enough injuries, they just lost yet another key players for the year, as linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has gone down with a season-ending shoulder injury. Edmunds popped up on the injury report this week with the shoulder issue, but it didn't appear to be too big of a deal. Evidently, it was more serious than initially anticipated. Now, the Giants have lost the anchor of their linebacking corps, the man they signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in free agency back in March. New York's run defense was already struggling as it was, so to subtract Edmunds on top of that will make things that much more challenging for Big Blue. Micah McFadden will now step back into a starting role, and fortunately, he has long proven to be serviceable — but he is a definitive downgrade from Edmunds. This injury changes absolutely everything for the Giants. Edmunds' absence will now put that much more pressure on rookie Arvell Reese, and it also means that Reese's mentor will no longer be on the field with him. Reese has looked spectacular in certain moments this year, but he has also looked very much like a first-year player at other times, so losing Edmunds will unquestionably have an effect on the youngster. And of course, it will also give running backs yet even more of a chance to break through the Giants' linebacking corps and into the defensive backfield. New York has now lost two of its top defensive players in Edmunds and Brian Burns, which is beyond devastating for a unit that displayed so much potential during the season opener. The Giants are now incredibly thin on that side of the ball, and in an NFC East that is totally up for grabs, New York may slowly be losing its advantage. To make matters worse, the schedule is about to get tougher. The Giants will face the suddenly hot Houston Texans on the road on Sunday before heading into their bye week. Then, New York will begin a difficult stretch that runs all the way through Week 18. Even in such a horrendous division, it's becoming harder and harder to view the Giants as a potential playoff team given all of their injuries. First, Jaxson Dart . Then Burns. Now Edmunds. It continues to snowball.

away.headline: Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries
away.blurb: Thomas, who has sat out Wednesday and Thursday over the past several weeks and returned to practice on a limited basis on Friday and Saturday before being cleared to play, is someone to watch this week. Last week he came out of the game just before the big fourth-quarter comeback attempt against the Saints; the veteran left tackle was visibly laboring through his groin injury throughout the game. Starting safety Jevon Holland was spotted at practice, off to the side with a trainer. Newsome and Holland have been the Giants defensive secondary’s best players so far this season, so hopefully their absences aren’t serious enough to keep them out of Sunday’s game. Speaking of the cornerback position, Newsome did not practice, but rookie Colton Hood (concussion) did. Sills, 6-foot-6 and 325 pounds, was originally an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma State whom the Eagles signed in 2022. That season, Sills, who has played guard in his short NFL career, was one of three undrafted free agents to make the Eagles roster but only appeared in one game for Philadelphia. Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries Skip to main content SI.COM The New York Giants will face one of the best defenses on Sunday when they travel to Houston to meet the Texans. So it was a bit alarming that on Wednesday, the team’s top three offensive tackles were not practicing. Starters Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and swing tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) were not participating in practice during the media viewing period. Eluemunor missed last week’s game as well with his injury after saying he would test it to see if he could anchor; he is also someone to watch this week. And with MBow now nursing something, the Giants could be thin at offensive tackle if he can’t play. The Texans have league sack leader Will Anderson, Jr. on one side of their formation and Danielle Hunter on the other. That would be quite the test for rookie J.C. Davis, who would presumably play left tackle; at right tackle, the Giants could potentially move Sisi Mauigoa from right guard to tackle, the position he played in college. Edmunds, Newsome Not Spotted During Media Viewing Portion of Practice Inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) were not spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. If Edmunds can’t go, Micah McFadden would get the start. The question then becomes who would wear the radio in his helmet: rookie Arvell Reese, the most likely candidate, or someone else. Rookie Colton Hood (concussion), receiver Darnell Mooney (neck), safety Tyler Nubin (neck), and tight end Theo Johnson (neck) were spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. Paulson Adebo’s Practice Window Opens Cornerback Paulson Adebo’s 21-day practice window is now open. If he clears, he could fill the roster vacancy left after Tuesday’s release of running back Najee Harris and defensive lineman Jihad Ward. Adebo has been on IR since Week 2

He admitted that "without a doubt" it isn't easy to no longer have a starting role. "Whenever you're used to something, you've had a taste of the pie, I guess, and then you don't get to go out there and eat with your boys anymore, it's tough, but I think it's just about staying present," McFadden said. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The Cardinals produce another improbable victory behind a barrage of field goals, and the Dolphins finally hold their first lead of the season Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League and the kickoff to Week 7 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Meanwhile, the Arizona Cardinals may be 2-4, but they're coming off a huge divisional victory over the Los Angeles Rams. The Cardinals are feeling it right now, and they're at home — but we know how Broncos Country travels, especially in the desert. At 4-2, the Broncos can't afford a slip-up — not if they want to keep pace with the Kansas City Chiefs in the division, and make their Week 8 rematch at Mile High a potential chance to get back to the top of the division, depending on what happens this Sunday with the Seattle Seahawks. That's me looking past the Cardinals a little bit. The Broncos won't be doing that. Sean Payton knows how to keep a team's focus on whichever game and opponent is up next, and that's the Cardinals. How will this one shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff see Sunday's action unfolding in Glendale, AZ. Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 4-2 : Getting Bo Nix back in the flow of things has become like a quest for the Holy Grail. All the internal tinkering on Nix might not be as important as facing a Cardinals team the Broncos should beat. While most eyes will be focused on how Nix performs, it's returning rookie running back Jonah Coleman who steals the limelight with two scores. Pick : Broncos 31, Cardinals 21 Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 4-2 : The Broncos' coaches and players are buzzing about a Nix breakout game. Looking at the Cardinals' 31st-ranked scoring defense — a unit allowing 350.5 yards per game — this is about as golden a get-right opportunity Nix could hope for. Courtland Sutton said , "At some point, the tide's going to turn" for Nix and this offense, and it happens at State Farm Stadium on Sunday. Nix passes for three touchdowns and 280 yards, while the Broncos romp in the desert. Pick : Broncos 27, Cardinals 17 Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 4-2 : Only speaking for myself, the Broncos haven’t yet earned the benefit of the doubt. Not yet. But if there’s any way to earn that — and any day to have a get-right game — it’s Sunday against the Cardinals. This goes for the offense more so than the defense, which has been fantastic of late. If not now for Nix, then when? Go out there and dominate, and those “confidence issues” will miraculously disappear. I foresee a better showing, though maybe not quite the 2018 Kick Your A** blowout. This is an inferior opponent who, quite frankly, the Broncos should handily dispatch. “Should.” Pick : Broncos 30, Cardinals 16 Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 4-2 : The Broncos' offense has been the source of much consternation. Is Nix hurt? Has the game passed Sean Payton by? Luckily, the Cardinals appear to be a get-right game. It's the NFL; there is no such thing as a guaranteed victory, but I expect the Broncos' defense and special teams, as well as continuity across the organization, to be felt in Arizona. I don't think the offense looks great... and even if it does, it's just one game, and the broader sample size should hold more weight in the total evaluation. Still, it will be nice to provide the fan base some hope. Pick : Broncos 20, Cardinals16 Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 4-2 : It's easy to think the Broncos will have their way with the Cardinals. Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? This spread suggests we could see a close game, so let’s dive right into my score prediction for this Week 7 battle. Broncos vs. Cardinals Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Broncos -4.5 (-110) Cardinals +4.5 (-110) Broncos: -230 Cardinals: +190 43.5 (Over -115/Under -105) This line has held steady since it opened , as the Broncos are still favored on the road by 4.5 points despite Arizona’s win over the Rams in Week 6. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The Cardinals are ninth in success rate and 15th in EPA/Play on offense, yet they’ve still scored 21 or fewer points in three of their six games. I expect Brissett to have a much tougher time against a Denver pass defense that – without Pat Surtain II – dominated Seattle and Los Angeles in back-to-back weeks. On the other side of the ball, how can anyone bet on Denver to put up points? The UNDER has hit in five of the Broncos’ six games this season, partially due to the fact that they’ve scored 23 or fewer points in five games and 20 or fewer points in four games. In this article, you'll find my favorite prop bets. Let's dive into them. Broncos vs. Cardinals Best NFL Prop Bets Odds via BetMGM Sportsbook Bo Nix OVER 1.5 Passing Touchdowns (+115) Michael Wilson OVER 4.5 Receptions (-115) Jaylen Waddle Anytime Touchdown (+200) In this week's edition of the Player Prop Countdown , I broke down why Bo Nix to throw for 2+ touchdowns is my favorite prop of Week 7: I understand the Bo Nix narrative heading into this week, but we have to cut him a little bit of slack. He has had to face a murderers' row of defenses this season, including the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, and Seahawks. He now gets to face by far the easiest defense he's faced this season. The Cardinals rank 30th in opponent dropback EPA, 25th in opponent dropback success rate, and they've allowed 16 passing touchdowns, the most in the NFL. At plus-money, I'll jump all over him to throw for at least two scores on Sunday. Michael Wilson has been having an underrated season thus far. If the Broncos take an early lead, the Cardinals will have to go to the air even more, giving Wilson plenty of opportunities to haul in 5+ receptions. Jaylen Waddle has nine more receptions than any other wide receiver on the Denver Broncos, and now he gets to face a Cardinals' defense that's in the bottom 10 in virtually every single pass defense metric. That could lead to big things for Waddle, who is due for another touchdown after having scored just one through his first six games as a Bronco. He's a great bet to score on Sunday at 2-1 odds. away.headline: Pat Surtain injury: Latest updates for Broncos cornerback
away.blurb: Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain went down with a non-contact ankle injury late in the second quarter of Sunday's game against the San Francisco 49ers . He was ruled out in the third quarter. After sitting out Sunday's game, Pat Surtain told the Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson that he wasn't really close to playing in Week 7. When asked if he could return in Week 8 against the Chiefs, Surtain said, "Possibly." Broncos CB Pat Surtain is inactive and will miss his third straight game. However, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport tweeted on Sunday that " there's a good chance " Surtain will be able to return against the Chiefs in Week 8. Broncos CB Pat Surtain questionable for Week 7 Denver's injury report for Sunday's game against Arizona has cornerback Pat Surtain officially listed as questionable . If he can't play, Jahdae Barron will likely be the next man up. Despite returning to practice on Wednesday, Pat Surtain seems more likely to return in Week 8 against the Chiefs, according to James Palmer of NFL on Prime Video . We'll see how the week goes for PS2. Pat Surtain might not return in Week 7 In an updated report on Pat Surtain's status, James Palmer of Prime Video clarified that PS2's injury was not a non-contact injury — it actually happened one play before the cornerback went down on the field. Palmer also reported that " [i]t might be tough " for Surtain to return to action in Week 7, suggesting PS2 might be more likely to return in Week 8. Pat Surtain ruled out for Week 6; there's hope for possible Week 7 return Pat Surtain has been ruled out for a Thursday Night Football clash with the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6, but there is hope he might be able to return against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7, according to KUSA-TV's Mike Klis . Pat Surtain avoids IR; ruled out for Week 5 ESPN's Adam Schefter said on Altitude Sports Radio that his guess is that Pat Surtain will land on injured reserve , which would rule the cornerback out for at least four games. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported this morning that Pat Surtain is expected to miss time, but it's not believed to be season-ending. "You hope it is just a couple weeks, maybe it ends up in an IR stint, but not expected to be season-ending," Rapoport said . If Surtain is placed on injured reserve, he would have to sit out at least four games. Broncos CB Pat Surtain ruled out Broncos cornerbacks Pat Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs), who were both originally listed as questionable to return, have been announced as ruled out for the rest of today's game. Riley Moss and Jahdae Barron are the two outside cornerbacks with Ja'Quan McMillian playing in the slot. Behind them on Denver's depth chart , the Broncos also have Kris Abrams-Draine. With PS2 sidelined, the team is down to four healthy cornerbacks on the active roster. Update : Moss (ribs) was announced as questionable to return after halftime, so Denver now has Barron and Abrams-Draine starting at the two outside cornerback spots. Surtai

away.headline: Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return
away.blurb: Running back Jonah Coleman, who has been designated to return from IR with his ankle injury, practiced in full on Wednesday. Patrick Surtain II, who left the team's Week 4 game with an ankle injury, was also at practice on a limited basis: Unfortunately, Tyler Badie, Talanoa Hufanga, and Jonah Elliss all did not practice, and Elliss' injury could end up being more extended. Hufanga hurt his ankle in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Chargers, and both Badie and Elliss got hurt in Week 6 against the Seattle Seahawks. Fortunately, Hufanga's injury is minor. As for Surtain, James Palmer is reporting that the likely return for the Defensive Player of the Year is Week 8 against Kansas City, but he also didn't totally shut the door on Surtain playing this week : Him practicing in limited fashion does give him a chance to play, but you almost want to wonder if the Broncos understand the opponents they have coming up and want to ease Surtain back into things for Week 8, as that game could carry major impact across the division and conference in terms of seeding. All in all, the Broncos seem to be trending toward being more 'full strength' for the Chiefs game in Week 8. However, not only could Coleman find his way back into the lineup in Week 7, but, until he's ruled out, Surtain could be nearing a return as well. The Broncos also have wide receiver Pat Bryant on IR. He is eligible to return f in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Denver plays Arizona, Kansas City, and Carolina before the Week 10 bye, which just so happens to line up nicely with the trade deadline. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return . The Denver Broncos have dealt with their share of injuries this year, unfortunately. The bright side though, is that the Broncos are consistently among the least-injured teams in the NFL, and the ailments this year have largely been minor. As the middle of the season approaches, the playoff race will slowly start to heat up, and Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs could present a legitimate playoff atmosphere. Before the Chiefs, though, the Broncos have to get by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. And in the team's first injury report of the week, it does seem to indicate that the team could get some key players back. away.headline: Cardinals get troubling Jeremiyah Love injury update before Broncos game
away.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses. away.headline: Is Jaylen Waddle Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Broncos vs. Cardinals in NFL Week 7)
away.blurb: Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle was limited in practice this week with a chest injury before logging a full session on Friday. Jaylen Waddle (chest) said he is good to go for Sunday's game at Arizona after being limited in practice the previous two days. Via @christomasson pic.twitter.com/HxpBUEsUmp Is Jaylen Waddle Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Broncos vs. Cardinals in NFL Week 7) Skip to main content ON SI He's now officially off the injury report and expected to play in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals. Waddle briefly left Denver's Week 6 win on Thursday night against the Seattle Seahawks, but he returned to the game in the second half. The Broncos star had four catches in the win, though the entire Denver passing offense has struggled this season. Bo Nix has not gotten going under center, and it's led to a rather pedestrian stat line for Waddle. He has 38 targets on the season, yet he's turned them into just 22 catches for 228 yards and a score. Waddle also has two carries for 23 yards. Outside of a big Week 2 against Jacksonville (eight catches 138 yards), Waddle has 35 or fewer receiving yards in every other game. Denver traded a first-round pick to Miami for Waddle in the offseason, so at some point the team needs to get him going with Nix at quarterback. This week, the SI Betting team has a player prop for both Nix and Waddle in Sunday's matchup with the two-win Cards. Best Broncos Prop Bet vs. Cardinals in NFL Week 7 Jaylen Waddle Anytime TD (+200) This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite props in his Player Prop Countdown column , and he’s targeting Bo Nix to toss multiple touchdown passes. He also shared his favorite props for this game, and he believes Waddle is worth a look to score: Jaylen Waddle has nine more receptions than any other wide receiver on the Denver Broncos, and now he gets to face a Cardinals' defense that's in the bottom 10 in virtually every single pass defense metric. That could lead to big things for Waddle, who is due for another touchdown after having scored just one through his first six games as a Bronco. He's a great bet to score on Sunday at 2-1 odds. home.headline: Cardinals get troubling Jeremiyah Love injury update before Broncos game
home.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses. home.headline: Broncos Get Mixed Pat Surtain II Injury News Ahead of Cardinals Game
home.blurb: But there is encouraging news about when the two-time All-Pro could return. However, Rapoport reported there is a good chance Surtain will return next week when the Broncos face the Kansas City Chiefs in an important AFC West matchup. Surtain was a limited participant in all three practices this week, and the Broncos listed him as questionable on Friday's final injury report. He has not yet been officially ruled out against Arizona. Safety Talanoa Hufanga has been ruled out against Arizona because of an ankle injury, continuing the secondary's recent injury problems . Although Surtain is unlikely to face Arizona, the possibility of his return against Kansas City would be a significant boost ahead of a key AFC West matchup. Broncos Get Mixed Pat Surtain II Injury News Ahead of Cardinals Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Broncos Get Mixed Pat Surtain II Injury News Ahead of Cardinals Game (IMAGN IMAGES) brianburden Sun, October 25, 2026 at 1:44 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Denver Broncos appear headed for another game without star cornerback Pat Surtain II. Surtain, who has missed Denver's last two games with an ankle injury, is unlikely to play Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . The update comes after Surtain returned to practice Wednesday for the first time since suffering a non-contact ankle injury during Denver's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Oct. 4. The injury initially raised significant concerns because Surtain went down without contact late in the first half against San Francisco. However, the Broncos subsequently received encouraging news about the injury , with NFL Network's Tom Pelissero reporting that Surtain's Achilles tendon was intact. Surtain missed Denver's 23-17 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Oct. 11 and its 17-14 overtime win against the Seattle Seahawks on Oct. 15. The Broncos have relied on their depth in the secondary during his absence. Denver previously elevated two cornerbacks from its practice squad after injuries sidelined Surtain and fellow starter Riley Moss. Moss, who suffered a rib injury against San Francisco, returned against Seattle and played 20 defensive snaps. He practiced fully throughout this week and carries no injury designation for Sunday's game, giving Denver an important boost even if Surtain remains sidelined. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine have also taken on larger responsibilities in the secondary, while Ja'Quan McMillian has continued handling the slot cornerback position. Denver's defensive depth remains under pressure elsewhere. The Broncos enter Sunday's matchup at 4-2 after consecutive victories, while the Cardinals are 2-4.

The Packers, winners of three in a row, are coming off a 23-13 defeat of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. Meanwhile, Detroit, which spent Week 6 on its bye, defeated the Arizona Cardinals in Week 5, 45-21. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 7 matchup with Green Bay. Christian Booher The Lions have their first chance to prove themselves in the NFC North Sunday, taking on a Green Bay Packers team that appears to be built to exploit Detroit's biggest weakness. Quarterback Jordan Love has been unafraid to test defenses down the field with wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. As a result, I think the Lions will try to dial up the pass-rush and try to get to Love before he has a chance to cut it loose. Offensively, the Lions need to get Jahmyr Gibbs going as the Packers did a good job of keeping him in check in their two meetings last year. Quarterback Jared Goff has been turnover-free through five games, and will need to keep that going to give his team the best chance to win. While the Lions have the ability to keep up in the event this game becomes a shootout, the Packers are uniquely equipped to attack the Lions' issues in coverage, both in the secondary and at linebacker. Green Bay makes one more play than Detroit, and hands Dan Campbell's team a crushing loss to start a crucial two-game stretch. Packers 31, Lions 28 The Detroit Lions have a big time test ahead of themselves on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. The Packers not only are red hot and winners of three in a row. But they're also due to receive a big boost to their run game with the return of Pro Bowl back Josh Jacobs. In addition, Green Bay receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are playing some of the best football of their NFL careers. Consequently, Kelvin Sheppard's defense won't have it easy in this Week 7 divisional affair. Yet, the Lions' defense will be in the best shape it's been all season due to the return of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch. He should provide a major boost to the team's secondary and put it in a stronger position to limit the productivity of Watson and Golden. I think Detroit's pass defense holds up just enough and Jared Goff and the offense come through in the fourth quarter, leading Dan Campbell's squad to its fourth victory of the season. Lions 31, Packers 24 John Maakaron The Lions return to action after a much needed week off. The Packers are visiting Ford Field missing a few key players, but will have running back Josh Jacobs in the lineup. If the defensive line can have another strong performance, Jordan Love will not have ample time to find his key targets. Tight end Tucker Kraft could be in line for a big game, but Detroit’s offense should keep the momentum from the first quarter of the season rolling. Sam LaPorta might just also have himself a productive afternoon, given the noise he created and wanting to prove he deserves a lucrative new contract. Emmett Matasovsky The Lions start divisional play with the Green Bay Packers this week, and it sees the return of Brian Branch and Josh Jacobs for their respective teams. That makes this week even more intriguing. It will be interesting to see how, or if, the bye week has given Detroit time to somewhat fix its porous secondary. The return of Branch will give fans a glimpse as to how this secondary should operate, but the boundary corner issues could make this discussion irrelevant. Green Bay is a hard team to gauge, even before factoring in the wild card element that it is a divisional game in the NFC North. The Lions, on fresh legs and with momentum, alongside a rowdy Ford Field crowd, take the win to open the second half of the season. The Packers are coming off a Sunday night home game. The Lions are coming off a Sunday at their homes with their bye week. So, Detroit – in a huge NFC North game, mind you, that could have playoff ramifications – has been given by the league a home game and a week of rest. Will it matter? Here are our predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Lions Prediction Since the start of the 2020 season, teams with a home game after their bye are 63-41, according to Stathead. That’s an enormous advantage. Will that alone decide the game? Probably not. But in a game between two quality teams – the Lions are 3.5-point favorites – it might not take much to be the tipping point. Eight consecutive games at Ford Field between the teams ended with a one-score differential; the last exception was in 2017, when Brett Hundley was the Packers’ quarterback. Both teams are going to score points. A lot of points. The over/under of 55.5 points is the highest on the board at FanDuel. The Lions on offense have been a well-oiled machine. It tallied 30 points in five of six games this season and is second in the league in scoring. Quarterback Jared Goff hasn’t thrown an interception all season. He is surrounded by probably the best quartet in the league with receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, running back Jahmyr Gibbs and tight end Sam LaPorta. Green Bay’s defense was great last week against the Dak Prescott-led Cowboys passing attack, but it didn’t have to contend with a back like Gibbs, who is arguably the best in the league – especially at home. The Packers have been hit and miss on offense – which is about what you’d expect for a team with a big-time quarterback and two big-play receivers but with an inconsistent offensive line and an unimaginably bad running game. The matchup is favorable, though, because the Lions’ defense has been terrible. It ranks 30th in points allowed and 32nd in total defense. At its current clip, it will threaten the 2011 Packers as the worst pass defense in NFL history. For the Lions, the best defense has been a good offense. They are 3-2 despite allowing 20 touchdowns. According to Stats Perform’s Opta data, they are the first team in NFL history to allow 20 offensive touchdowns and have a winning record through five games. Ultimately, three big issues stand the Packers’ way. One, they have struggled to protect Love. Well, the Lions lead the NFL in sacks even while playing one fewer game than most teams. Can Green Bay’s tackles overcome the noise to keep Aidan Hutchinson away from Love? Two, they have struggled to pressure the quarterback at times. Goff is an elite quarterback when given time. As coach Matt LaFleur said this week, “It’s hard for a quarterback to throw when he’s on his back.” Can the Packers put Goff on his back enough? Furthermore, the Green Bay defense will line up without Micah Parsons, Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin. And, finally, there’s this festering problem: The Packers have fatal flaws they haven’t solved. Love has been stymied by 19 drops; no other quarterback has more than 11. They lead the league in penalties and penalty yards. Love has faced the third-most pressures. “The simple stuff, whether from scheme-wise or the understanding of what we’re trying to get done, when you have some mistakes that can lead to negative plays, that’s the stuff we got to clean up and be better at,” Love said. It’s those things that will put the Packers at a disadvantage in every big game – no matter the location or scheduling quirk – until they get them fixed. Ultimately, the team that makes the fewest mistakes will win. Based on the first five games, it’s hard to believe that will be the Packers. Bill Huber’s Prediction: Lions 31, Packers 27. Bill’s Record: 3-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Lions Prediction The Packers have lost too many games like these in recent years, which have caused them to travel the long road in the postseason. In 2024, they lost all but one division game, which played a significant factor in them being the seventh seed in the NFC playoffs. Last year’s late-season debacle in Chicago essentially sealed their fate that the wild-card meeting rematch would be at Soldier Field instead of the friendly confines of Lambeau Field. Simply put, the Packers need to knock off the Lions on the road on Sunday to keep pace with those in front of them and remain in position to be a legitimate NFC North contender. In a game where points should be scored in bunches, one mistake could be the difference. Who do you trust more to play clean and disciplined? Dan Campbell's Lions or Matt LaFleur's Packers? That, combined with the Lions being at home off a bye, gives them the nod. Jacob’s Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 31 Jacob’s Record: 3-3. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. away.headline: Green Bay Packers RB Josh Jacobs contrite as he prepares to play again amid ongoing NFL investigation
away.blurb: The NFL is still investigating Jacobs over the incident, so the league still could hand out more discipline to the three-time Pro Bowl running back. But for now, Jacobs is eligible to play again for the Packers after missing the first six games of the season. “I thought I’d be playing sooner,” Jacobs said. “But, you know, the optics of everything, I understand the other side. For me, like I said, I’m just grateful to be able to play. It was one of them things where I didn’t want to sit the whole year and then figure it out. I’m just grateful to be back on the team and to be back playing.” Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email GREEN BAY — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs expressed contrition as he returned to practice Wednesday and talked with reporters for the first time since pleading no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground. “Obviously, man, I’m remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation,” Jacobs said. “Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur and a four-second, three-second decision can alter your life, honestly.” Jacobs was removed this week from the commissioner’s exempt list, which had prevented him from playing or practicing. The NFL had placed Jacobs on that list Aug. 30 , shortly after charges were filed against him . He pleaded no contest last month to misdemeanor counts of battery and criminal damage to property. The Packers (4-2) face the Lions on Sunday in Detroit. Jacobs was arrested May 26 , three days after police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, the woman told them that Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground. Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head. The criminal complaint against him noted that a surveillance video from the camera system in their garage corroborated the woman’s statement. Both Jacobs and the victim have gone to court attempting to have that video and other evidence sealed permanently . Jacobs declined to discuss the specifics of his case but said he hopes to use the situation as an opportunity to grow into a better person. “You never want to be in this situation, but just me being honest, for my life, it was probably one of the best things to ever happen to me,” Jacobs said. “I say that because it gave me a chance to sit down and reevaluate what’s important and what I want my life to look like, and what do I want people to know me for. away.blurb: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News Evan Siegle, packers.com LB Zaire Franklin GREEN BAY – Packers have officially ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) and listed four questionable for Sunday's NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. The Packers didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Jordan Love (back), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), and receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle). Lions safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participants in practice this week but are both questionable for Sunday. Ya-Sin was injured on special teams in Week 4, missed the Lions game in Week 5, but was able to get healthy enough to practice over the bye and was back on the practice field on Tuesday. C Cade Mays (Wrist) — Upgraded from limited practice S Brian Branch (Achilles) — Upgraded from limited practice As mentioned above, Mays and Branch are on track to return and start this week. home.headline: Packers Announce Jordan Love Injury News Before Lions Showdown
home.blurb: The Packers officially added Love to their injury report with a new back injury ahead of Sunday afternoon's game in Detroit and listed him as an estimated limited participant for their "jog-through" practice session on Wednesday, October 21. Who is Packers' Backup QB if Jordan Love Sits Out? The Packers are still a long few days away from being anywhere close to potentially ruling out Love for Week 7's road game against the Lions. Even so, it is worth examining their fallback plan at quarterback if Love's injury holds him out. The Packers would need to add Slovis to their 53-man roster to have him available as their emergency third quarterback against the Lions. They could also just elevate him and make him active, but that would leave three active quarterbacks — unless they become certain Love won't play. All four players were estimated limited participants for Wednesday's walkthrough. Defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles) was also a limited participant as he continues to work through his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve. Love — who is on the injury report for the first time this season — will have two more practices to improve his practice participation before the Packers must decide whether to list him with an injury designation on their final injury report. According to The Athletic's Matt Schneidman , though, Love said there is "no chance" he won't play against the Lions despite dealing with back soreness. Well, anyone backing the Raiders in Week 7 has a lot more company, with a good chunk of the experts giving them a real shot against the Rams Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Covering the spread against Buffalo apparently buys a team some respect. The computer models still like the Rams comfortably, but some of the humans are far less sure, and a few of them switched sides from last week. Even the Raiders Wire staff is on board too, picking the Raiders 3-1 with an average score of 27-25. NFL.com's panel can barely agree Three of NFL.com's five analysts picked the Rams, with Jeremy Bergman at 24-17, Gennaro Filice at 27-24 and Dan Parr at 31-27. The other two went with the Raiders, and both picks come with a story. Bobby Kownack had the Bills hanging 35 points on the Raiders last week. Now he has the Raiders winning a 17-14 rock fight , which is quite a change of heart in seven days. Brooke Cersosimo has the Raiders by one at 25-24, and the Rams clearly gave her more to think about than she expected. "Of all the teams in the league, I would not have guessed the Rams would give me pause at this point in the season," Cersosimo wrote. She also has the game ending on a Raiders field goal in the final minute. Bleacher Report's experts traded seats The funniest twist came from Bleacher Report. Maurice Moton was the panel's lone Raiders backer last week, and this week he jumped to the Rams, while Gary Davenport, who doubted the Raiders against Buffalo, came over to their side. "Why lay this many points on the road against a Raiders team that just covered the same spread against Buffalo?" Davenport wrote. Moton expects the Rams to adjust without Davante Adams by leaning on their tight ends. The panel finished 4-3 in favor of the Raiders against a 4.5-point spread, with Ian Hanford, Wes O'Donnell and Brent Sobleski joining Davenport. "They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here," Prisco wrote. "But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders, who hang around." The rest of the CBS panel split 4-3 for the Rams against the spread, with Tyler Sullivan and Jamey Eisenberg standing with Prisco. Meanwhile, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio has the Rams winning 26-23 and sees a season on the line for Los Angeles. "If the Rams get to five losses with 10 games left, they could be done," Florio wrote. The computers aren't buying it The models are far more confident than we (humans). Dimers gives the Rams a 70.8% chance to win with a 26-20 projection, and the Covers AI model has Los Angeles winning 27-20. Five of the seven human score predictions in this roundup land within three points, though. These experts expect another one-score game, and the Raiders have lost two of their last three games by a field goal. away.headline: Rams Week 7 injury report vs. Raiders: Where Davante Adams, Puka Nacua injuries leave LA offense
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders without Davante Adams and with another major question surrounding Puka Nacua . Adams is out, while Nacua is questionable with a calf injury after missing Friday’s practice. That combination leaves Los Angeles preparing for two different offensive scenarios: building around an available Nacua or operating without either receiver. Neither offers the flexibility the Rams would have with both in the lineup. The concern extends beyond redistributing targets. Losing receiving options can change defensive coverage, third-down decisions and red-zone planning. With Adams unavailable, Nacua’s status becomes the biggest remaining variable in determining how aggressively Los Angeles can attack through the air. Nacua had no injury listing Wednesday, was limited Thursday and did not participate Friday. That progression raises concern because his involvement decreased before the final report, although it does not establish the injury’s severity or confirm he will miss kickoff. His questionable designation leaves the possibility of playing open. It does not guarantee a normal workload if he is active. The underlying objective would be keeping the offense ahead of the chains. Third-and-long becomes harder when established receiving options are unavailable and defenses can concentrate attention elsewhere. Los Angeles also has uncertainty on defense. Cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable with a groin injury after missing all three practices. Inside linebacker Nate Landman is out with a concussion following three nonparticipation listings. For the offense, the takeaway is straightforward: Adams’ absence reduces its options, and Nacua’s availability determines how extensive the adjustment becomes. Los Angeles needs a sustainable plan for either outcome, not an assumption that questionable means ready for an unrestricted workload. His status should therefore be separated from Nacua’s documented calf issue rather than treating both situations as identical. Nacua’s production illustrates what is at stake. The Rams list him with 37 receptions for 417 yards and one receiving touchdown across four appearances this season. That represents substantial production to potentially remove from an already depleted receiving group. If Nacua plays, Los Angeles must balance using its remaining centerpiece with whatever workload he can handle. If he sits, the passing game requires a broader redistribution rather than simply transferring Adams’ opportunities to one replacement.
