away.headline: Rams receiver opens up about Davante Adams injury, stepping into spotlight
away.blurb: “I’ve learned a lot from those guys. I appreciate the heck out of them,” Mumpfield said. “They speak life into me all the time, just saying what they believe I can do and what I’m capable of.” LAS VEGAS — Konata Mumpfield has spent the season learning from two of the NFL’s most dangerous wide receivers. Now, with the Los Angeles Rams’ season teetering on the brink, the young receiver is being asked to put those lessons to work. And Mumpfield’s opportunity comes at a heartbreaking price. With superstar receiver Davante Adams sidelined for six to 10 weeks after rupturing his hamstring, and All-Pro Puka Nacua battling lingering calf and groin injuries , Mumpfield suddenly finds himself thrust into a starring role for a Rams offense desperately searching for answers. But for Mumpfield, losing Adams is about much more than football. “With Tae [Davante Adams] going down, it crushes me because I know how much it means to him,” Mumpfield told The California Post in an exclusive interview. “He’s a big brother and mentor to me.” Adams has spent the season taking Mumpfield under his wing, teaching him the finer details of route running, recognizing defensive coverages and identifying the subtle tells that separate good receivers from great ones. From Nacua, the lesson has been considerably less complicated. The All-pro receiver has taught Mumpfield about being more physical after catching the football. How you can make opposing defenders pay for trying to tackle you. “I just kind of try to model my mindset after him,” Mumpfield said. “When I catch the ball, make them tackle me.” That physical mentality could prove invaluable Sunday against a Raiders defense that has struggled to limit yards after the catch. Mumpfield flashed his potential earlier this season against Denver, but with the Rams sitting at 2-4 and buried in last place in the NFC West , occasional flashes won’t be enough anymore. Matthew Stafford needs dependable targets. Sean McVay needs his offense to stop sleepwalking through the opening three quarters. And the Rams need victories before their playoff aspirations become nothing more than wishful thinking. “Definitely this week, just trying to make sure we’re on the same page and I’m understanding what he’s seeing,” Mumpfield said of developing chemistry with Stafford. Despite the injuries, Mumpfield remains confident the Rams have enough talent to stay afloat and fight their way back into playoff contention. “I think it’s just expected,” he said of the receiving corps stepping up. “All of us have extreme capabilities in this room.” He pointed to Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Brennan Presley and CJ Daniels as players capable of answering the call. “We believe in Tutu. We believe in J-Whitt. We believe in Brennan Presley. We believe in CJ Daniels,” Mumpfield said. “It’s just expected.” Against Las Vegas, his approach is equally straightforward. “You want to be on the attack. You don’t want to let things come to you.” California Post News: Fa

Neither offers the flexibility the Rams would have with both in the lineup. The concern extends beyond redistributing targets. With Adams unavailable, Nacua’s status becomes the biggest remaining variable in determining how aggressively Los Angeles can attack through the air. Cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable with a groin injury after missing all three practices. Inside linebacker Nate Landman is out with a concussion following three nonparticipation listings. For the offense, the takeaway is straightforward: Adams’ absence reduces its options, and Nacua’s availability determines how extensive the adjustment becomes. Los Angeles needs a sustainable plan for either outcome, not an assumption that questionable means ready for an unrestricted workload. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. It won’t happen again. Personality-wise, I’m not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills are bringing back a familiar face with cornerback Tre’Davious White agreeing to sign to the team’s practice squad, a person with knowledge of discussions told The Associated Press. This weekend, Seattle will host the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. Kansas City is coming off a frustrating 2025 campaign, which ended with a record of 6-11. That was the first time they had a losing season under Andy Reid, and they've already turned things around. Much of that is due to Kenneth Walker III, the former Seahawk who has been electric for the Chiefs . Seattle needs to find a way to contain Walker, while also figuring out how to get their ground game on track, which could happen with Zach Charbonnet set to return to action. If they can do that, they will have a chance to score the upset. As the game nears, let's see who the experts believe will walk away with the win this weekend. "The Chiefs, who’ve never fielded a top-15 rushing attack during Mahomes’ time as a starter, rank second with an average of 159.8 ground yards per game," Kownack wrote. "Walker leads the league with 665 rushing yards -- and that’s despite the fact that he’s played one fewer game than the next three leading rushers (Bijan Robinson, James Cook III and Derrick Henry), thanks to K.C.’s Week 5 bye. Meanwhile, the Seahawks have yet to finish a game with a 100-yard rusher, and their well-documented struggles on the ground are putting too much on Sam Darnold’s plate, as evidenced by the quarterback’s seven interceptions in the past four weeks." picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Seahawks: NFL Week 7 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Kansas City Chiefs are back in prime time this weekend, taking center stage at Lumen Field in a matter of hours against a feisty Seattle Seahawks squad that's still finding its way a bit after winning the Super Bowl earlier this calendar year. Don't let the home team's offensive struggles fool you, though, as this remains one of the premier clubs in the NFL. Head coach Mike Macdonald's group might have the game's best wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and the Seahawks' defense is in the conversation for being football's most elite unit once again. Kansas City has its work cut out for it in what could be a tough road game, but one thing this year's team has shown is an abundance of grit. Will Sunday Night Football be more of the same? How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 7 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: Between the Seahawks’ offensive inconsistencies and the Chiefs’ offensive injuries, this feels like a low-scoring, wire-to-wire affair between two teams with elite elements in some areas and significant questions in others. Ultimately, fitting the narrative of the week perfectly, Kenneth Walker should be the key to this game for both teams. Jordan Foote: Going into Seattle and securing a win is easily the toughest ask of the Chiefs through the first month-and-a-half of the season. The Seahawks' defense, even while banged up, is amazing. On the other side of the ball, however, there's next to no run game. That's had a negative impact on quarterback Sam Darnold, who also isn't sniffing the production he found a season ago. Week 7's tilt could go either way, but I'll side with the offense I believe in much more. Minus wideout Rashee Rice and right tackle Jaylon Moore , look for this one to be a statement game for one or both of quarterback Patrick Mahomes and running back Kenneth Walker III in hostile territory. Joshua Schulman: Kenneth Walker is set to return to face the franchise he won a Super Bowl with less than nine months ago, and he'll be looking to make his former team regret letting him walk. He and Jaxon Smith-Njigba headline one of the most exciting Sunday Night Football contests in recent memory. There's a generational quarterback in Patrick Mahomes squaring off against a generational defense that has picked up where it left off a season ago, despite the offense's inconsistencies. Seattle's slow start has actually placed it out of the playoff picture, and a home loss before another prime-time showdown against the Bears would be disastrous. I think the Seahawks understand the importance of this matchup and will take advantage of their 10 days of rest. Given the Chiefs' shaky kicking game and a lack of proven offensive weapons outside of Walker in what should be a low-scoring contest, I think Mike Macdonald and Co. narrowly steal one to hand Kansas City its first loss. Tyler Brown: This one has the look of a defensive rock fight. Seattle’s passing defense ranks first in the NFL, allowing just 141 yards per game, and Kansas City’s defense has held opponents under 20 points in most of its wins. The ingredients are there for a low-scoring grind from start to finish. That said, the Chiefs are the number one offense in the NFL for a reason. Seattle’s defense may be able to slow down Walker or Mahomes, but doing both simultaneously is a different ask entirely. If the run game gets going, the play-action attack opens up. If Mahomes starts finding his receivers, the box opens up for Walker. At some point, one of those two is going to win. On the other side, if Sam Darnold can buy time in the pocket, Smith-Njigba is going to get loose. The Chiefs’ defense just has to make sure that happens once or twice rather than repeatedly. away.blurb: Tyreek Hill’s potential return to the Kansas City Chiefs has hit a significant roadblock, leaving fans wondering whether the explosive wide receiver will wear the red and gold again. What once looked like a promising reunion has lost momentum as concerns over his recovery continue to shape the conversation. With the Chiefs winning games and Patrick Mahomes leading the offence, Kansas City faces a difficult choice: take a chance on a familiar star or trust the players already on the roster. For Hill, the bigger challenge remains proving he can return to the field at his best. Without a clear medical assessment and a confirmed return timeline, Kansas City may be unwilling to take that risk. Get breaking news anytime, anywhere. Download the TOI app now! Why the Chiefs are hesitant to sign Tyreek Hill However, Hill’s health remains the biggest obstacle. The 32-year-old suffered a dislocated left knee and multiple ligament tears while playing for the Miami Dolphins during Week 4 of the 2025 NFL season. His injury required two surgeries, making his road back to professional football particularly challenging. Hill’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has offered encouraging updates about his client’s rehabilitation and readiness to explore opportunities with NFL teams. Yet positive training reports cannot replace the medical assessments teams need before committing to a player recovering from such a serious injury. Hill built his reputation on elite speed, sharp changes of direction and the ability to turn short passes into game-changing plays. Those qualities make him dangerous, but they also raise questions about how quickly he can regain his previous form. Andy Reid’s Tyreek Hill update offers little hope of a reunion The comments suggest Kansas City is not preparing to rush into a deal, despite the team's earlier need for additional receiving options. Mahomes has also given the Chiefs reason to remain patient. He has started the 2026 campaign strongly, distributing the ball to targets such as Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce. That production gives the coaching staff less reason to disrupt its current offensive plans for a player whose availability remains uncertain. Roster planning is another consideration. Bringing Hill back would require the team to assess his conditioning, recovery progress and ability to handle the demands of an NFL season. Promoting players who already understand Reid’s system could offer a more straightforward solution. Still, the situation could change if Kansas City suffers more injuries or Hill receives medical clearance sooner than expected. For now, Hill remains a free agent, and the Chiefs appear content to move forward without him. A reunion is not impossible, but the former Kansas City star must first overcome the uncertainty surrounding his recovery before any serious move becomes realistic. Steven Bisig-Imagn Images Charles Goldman Mon, October 26, 2026 at 4:23 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs escaped the Week 7 loss to the Seattle Seahawks relatively unscathed, which feels like something worth celebrating. There wasn't much to celebrate after the Kansas City Chiefs' 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, but the injury situation might actually be one of those things. The team was missing several pieces in Week 7, with Tyquan Thornton, Rashee Rice, Jaylon Moore, and Josh Simmons among the injured starters. Another starter on defense got banged up during the game, but his injury doesn't appear to be anything serious. "There's not really any injuries to mention," Reid said, before mentioning the lone injury. " Nick (Bolton) had some spasms in his neck, and he'll work through that and be OK." Bolton played some inspired run defense against the Seahawks on Sunday, leading the team with six solo stops, 11 combined tackles, and a tackle for loss. He was dinged in the third quarter, missing just a single snap. Bolton returned to the game and made a play that forced a Seattle field goal, extending the lead to 13. He was staggered a bit later in the second half, but didn't leave the game. The good news is that Bolton doesn't appear to be at any risk of missing time. He's been a force on defense this year and remains the team's green dot and defensive play-caller. The Chiefs should be healthier when they face the Broncos in Week 8 The Chiefs will look to bounce back against an AFC West rival in Week 8. It won't be easy as they travel to Mile High Stadium to face the Denver Broncos, but the team should be healthier for this game. Jaylon Moore will have a chance to clear the NFL's concussion protocol during practice this week. They need him at right tackle for this one because Joshua Ezeudu struggled in his first start. home.blurb: The Seahawks will be without running back Zach Charbonnet for another game. Charbonnet, who is working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in the Divisional Round of the playoffs, practiced fully this week, but has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Also ruled out for the Seahawks are linebacker Drake Thomas , who will be out for the second week in a row due to an ankle injury, and linebacker Chazz Surratt , who will be missing a fourth straight game with a calf injury. Among those listed as questionable for the Seahawks is safety Nick Emmanwori , who was a new addition to the injury report on Friday, listed as limited due to a hip. Also questionable are outside linebackers DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and Uchenna Nwosu (hip), both of whom were limited for the second straight day, backup quarterback Drew Lock , who has been limited all week with a right elbow injury, and outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (hamstring), who was limited Friday after not practicing the previous two days. For the Chiefs, starting right tackle Jaylon Moore is out due to a concussion. Left tackle Josh Simmons, who already missed the first five games of the season with a back injury, was placed on injured reserve earlier this week. Also out for Kansas City are receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and running back Brashard Smith (hamstring). For the Chiefs, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) and linebacker Cooper Macdonald (knee) are both listed as questionable after being limited in Friday's practice. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . away.headline: Can Eagles injured offense beat Cowboys D? Our experts score predictions
away.blurb: The Eagles' offense has proceeded to get only worse now that quarterback Jalen Hurts is lost for the season because of blood clots in both lungs, with Tanner McKee replacing him. And the Eagles will be without their top two wide receivers in DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, and running back Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable. It's possible that left guard Landon Dickerson will come off injured reserve, and center Drew Kendall could return as well after missing two games with a knee injury. The Eagles could be without edge rushers Jonathan Greenard and Nolan Smith, and possibly Jalyx Hunt. If they can't get pressure on QB Dak Prescott, it could be a long night for the Eagles' secondary against WRs CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. The only way the Eagles can pull this out is with a ball-control offense. If Barkley, Dickerson and Kendall are back, they can do it. Jalen Hurts is out for the season and Saquon Barkley hasn't played since Week 3. Thing is, it doesn't matter. The offensive line is porous. Even if Hurts and Barkley were there, the Eagles wouldn't be successful without the protection they've expected for years. And, without sustained drives on offense, the defense is gassed in the second half. The season is done. I'm sure the Eagles might win another game (I'm looking at you Arizona), but until the offensive line improves, it's hard to imagine a victory. And on Monday night at The Linc, expect an ugly evening as the hated Dallas Cowboys push the losing streak to five. The Eagles are at a low point, and lifting themselves out of it appears unlikely because those assigned the duties and paid the salaries to excel and win football games, coaches and players both, have utterly failed. And now comes a Monday night bout with despised Dallas for which it's difficult to summon any optimism the Eagles may actually rise to the occasion, despite the 2-4 Cowboys' own mediocrity. I respectfully disagree with the group (well, most of the group). As a proud member of Steelers Nation, I know rivalries bring out something different, especially on a big stage. I'm taking the Eagles over the Cowboys, and I fully expect the memes afterward to be glorious. The who-are-these-guys Iggles face the predictably disappointing Cowboys on a Monday Night Football game that should open with an old-school rendition of Dandy Don Meridith singing 'Turn out the Lights.' What happens when the moveable object meets a resistible force? Who cares? Can Eagles injured offense beat Cowboys D? home.blurb: Let's take a look at some of the injuries the Philadelphia Eagles have dealt with throughout the 2026 NFL season, looking at both sides of the ball and who is out short and long-term. To make matters worse, the Eagles have also been without running back Saquon Barkley since their Week 4 loss to the Rams. Barkley suffered a hamstring injury and has missed Philadelphia's last two games. He returned to practice on Thursday, October 22, for the first time since suffering the injury and was a limited participant. Barkley and the Eagles will be aiming for his return on Monday against the Cowboys, but his availability is still uncertain. Both pass catchers have missed time due to hamstring and knee injuries, respectively. Wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks, outside linebacker Nolan Smith and defensive back Michael Carter II also did not practice Thursday. Notable Injuries Throughout the Season Quarterback Jalen Hurts' recently diagnosed blood clots are easily the biggest injury storyline surrounding the Eagles this season. Hurts was placed on injured reserve on October 17 after doctors initially discovered a superficial blood clot in his left calf. Additional testing revealed deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both lungs, and he's now expected to miss the rest of the season as he undergoes approximately three months of blood thinner treatment. When healthy, Hurts is one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL, and his absence is a huge hit to an Eagles team that has already struggled this season.
